Task Description:
The churn model `churn-hgb-v3` scored an offline validation AUC of 0.805, but 0.656 in its first live month
(`/app/INCIDENT.md`). Its feature pipeline in `/app/churn` already uses only events stamped before each prediction
(`/app/CHANGELOG.md`), yet the live scoring service computed other values for the same predictions. The live service
computes every feature at the moment of a prediction from the warehouse tables as they stand at that moment
(`/app/live/features.py`). The pipeline builds its training table from an extract taken later (`/app/data`, this
brand's warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z). The tables are described in `/app/docs/WAREHOUSE.md`, the warehouse's own
records of its job runs and transactions are in `/app/data/_ops/`, and samples of what the live service computed are
in `/app/logs/`.

Fix `python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` (run from `/app`) so that, for every row of the
extract's `scoring_points.csv`, each feature is the value the live service would have computed for that customer at
that row's `as_of`, had it been running then against the warehouse as it stood at that moment (exactly the rows and
values committed to it before that moment, in the tables its queries name). This must hold for any extract with the
layout of `/app/data`. Keep every feature of `/app/live/features.py` whose live value the extract determines for every
row; leave out any feature whose live value the extract cannot determine for some rows.

How the result is checked:
- `python3 -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` is run from a copy of `/app` at another path, as
  an unprivileged user, on extracts of the company's other brands: the same seven CSV files, `_ops/` folder and layout
  as `/app/data`, about the same size and period, with other customers, events and load histories (their own job runs,
  failures and migrations). It must exit with status 0 and write the parquet file. Do not rely on network access, on
  absolute paths into `/app`, or on anything in `/app/data` or `/app/logs`.
- The output must have exactly one row per row of the extract's `scoring_points.csv`, with the columns `customer_id`,
  `as_of` and every kept feature, named as in `/app/live/features.py`. Extra columns, row order and column order do not
  matter, but a column named after a feature that should be left out fails unless all its values are null.
  `customer_id` may be any integer type; `as_of` a timestamp (time-zone aware, or naive meaning UTC) or an ISO 8601
  string; the integer features (`orders_7d`, `orders_30d`, `spend_30d_cents`, `tickets_30d`) any numeric type holding
  whole numbers; a null a parquet null or NaN.
- Every value must equal what the live service would have computed: integer features exactly, other numbers within
  1e-6 plus 1e-9 times the expected value, strings exactly, nulls exactly where the live service would have had no value.
- An extract is also changed in everything the warehouse did not yet hold at some cut time (in any table, whatever the
  date of the event a row records) and the command is run again: every prediction with `as_of` at or before the cut
  must keep the same feature values (within the tolerances above). The changed extract is still a copy of the
  warehouse at the same moment as the original extract, in the same layout; only what the warehouse did not yet hold
  at the cut differs, and its `_ops/` records match it: every record dated before the cut is unchanged, and the later
  records describe the changed extract.
- Each run is stopped after 60 seconds and then fails. The grading container has the same resources as this one
  (2 vCPUs, 4 GiB), and `/app/data` is about the size of the graded extracts, so time a run on it. Graded runs set
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`.
- `python -m churn.train` is not graded; it may help to check the work.

Only /app is kept when we grade: folders named `data`, `__pycache__` or `.venv` anywhere under /app are dropped, and the packages already installed are available.

# INC-2077: churn-hgb-v3 scores far worse live than in validation

Status: open. Owner: ML platform on-call. Opened 2026-03-04, updated 2026-03-05.

## What happened
- `churn-hgb-v3` is trained on the feature table that the offline pipeline builds (`churn/`, v3 in `CHANGELOG.md`).
  Built from this brand's extract (`data/`, the warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z), that table gives
  **offline validation AUC 0.805** in `python -m churn.train` (trained on the predictions before 2025-09-01,
  validated on those of 2025-09-01 to 2025-11-30).
- The model went live on 2026-01-01. The live scoring service computes the features of each request itself, from the
  warehouse at the moment of the request (`live/features.py`). On the 3,415 predictions of January 2026, whose 30-day
  outcomes have all landed in `labels`: **live AUC 0.656**.
- The model and its hyperparameters did not change between validation and launch.

## Tried so far
- Retrained with much stronger regularization and shallower trees (`--l2 50 --max-depth 2`): offline AUC 0.813. The
  offline number did not fall, so this is not ordinary overfitting.
- Compared the live service with `live/features.py` by hand on 200 January requests: the service computes exactly what
  its queries say.
- Pulled a random sample of about 10% of the requests of January 2026, with the values the service computed:
  `logs/live_2026-01_sample.jsonl`, 365 requests, one JSON object per line with `customer_id`, `as_of`, `trigger`, the
  11 `features` and the model's `score`.

## Next step (model team)
`churn-hgb-v4` is to be trained on a feature table that matches what the live service computed for every past
prediction. Every feature whose live value can be matched for every prediction is kept; any feature whose live value
cannot be matched is dropped from v4.

# Changelog: the offline feature pipeline (`churn/`)

## v3 (2025-12-19): the training table of churn-hgb-v3
Fixes INC-2041: in four places, v2 used events stamped at or after the prediction time `t`.
- `windows.py`: the order, spend and ticket windows are `[t - W days, t)` on the exact event timestamps. v2 summed
  whole UTC days, the day of `t` included, so events later on the prediction day were counted.
- `status.py`: the latest snapshot dated before `date(t)`. A snapshot dated D records the status at the end of day D;
  v2 took the customer's latest snapshot in the extract, which is often dated after `t`.
- `impute.py`: a missing `app_minutes_7d` takes the customer's most recent earlier reading only. v2 filled backward
  first, from a later reading.
- `encoding.py`: `te_district` counts only labels whose 30-day window had closed before `t` (`as_of + 30 days < t`),
  for the district and for the prior alike. v2 used every label in the extract, the prediction's own and later ones
  included.

Also in v3:
- `attributes.py` (new): `plan` and `days_since_last_login` from the customer record, the two features of the live
  service that v2 did not build. A last login at or after `t` is ignored (the feature is null then).
- `extract.py` loads the seven tables described in `docs/WAREHOUSE.md`.
- `train.py`: every column of the feature table other than `customer_id` and `as_of` is a model input, and string
  columns are one-hot encoded (v2 encoded `status` only); a column that holds no value at all is skipped.

"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>"""
import argparse
import os

from churn.attributes import days_since_last_login, plan
from churn.encoding import district_encoding
from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes
from churn.status import latest_status
from churn.windows import activity_features, tenure_days

FEATURE_COLUMNS = ["orders_7d", "orders_30d", "spend_30d_cents", "tickets_30d", "days_since_last_order",
                   "tenure_days", "status", "plan", "days_since_last_login", "app_minutes_7d", "te_district"]


def build(data_dir):
    t = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = t["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    feats = activity_features(points, t["orders"], t["tickets"])
    feats["tenure_days"] = tenure_days(points, t["customers"])
    feats["status"] = latest_status(points, t["status_snapshots"])
    feats["plan"] = plan(points, t["customers"])
    feats["days_since_last_login"] = days_since_last_login(points, t["customers"])
    feats["app_minutes_7d"] = fill_app_minutes(points)
    feats["te_district"] = district_encoding(points, t["labels"], t["customers"])
    return feats[["customer_id", "as_of"] + FEATURE_COLUMNS]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out)), exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Warehouse tables (churn scoring)

Written 2025-02-14 by the data platform for the warehouse and its nightly loaders as they were on that date, and not
updated since. The scheduler's own records of every job run and transaction, later changes included, are in each
extract's `_ops/` folder (below).

The seven tables below are the warehouse tables that the live scoring service (`live/features.py`) and the churn
pipeline (`churn/`) read. This page says what each table holds and which system writes it. Every brand of the company
runs the same warehouse and jobs; each brand's job runs, failures and changes are its own.

## Reading the warehouse
- A query that starts at a moment t sees exactly the rows and values committed before t: a row committed at or after
  t is not seen, and a value overwritten at or after t is seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of
  the event the row records.
- A query reads each table by the name it has when the query starts.
- `_loaded_at` is the commit time of the load that wrote the row; in `orders`, `_load_job` names that load.
- An extract is a copy of every table as the warehouse held it at one moment: the rows and values committed before
  that moment, with the `_ops/` records written before it.
- Timestamps are UTC, written as ISO 8601 with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds (`2025-02-04T06:00:00Z`);
  `snapshot_date` is a UTC date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); amounts are integer cents. Columns whose names start with `_` are
  written by the loaders, not by the source systems.

## The scheduler's records (`_ops/`)
- `_ops/scheduler.log` has one UTC event per line, `<time> <job> run=<run> <event>`: each task's start
  (`state=running`) and end (`state=success` or `state=failed`), and between them the lines the task writes, such as
  the rows it selected or copied, the transaction it sent (`sent txn <n> to commit`), the statements it ran and the
  checks it made.
- `_ops/commits.jsonl` has one JSON object per transaction a scheduled job sent: `txn`, `at`, `outcome` (`commit` or
  `rollback`), `table` and `rows` (the table the transaction writes rows into and how many; null for schema
  statements).
- `_ops/commits.jsonl` is the commit log of the scheduled jobs: a transaction is committed if and only if its outcome
  is `commit`, and it is committed at its `at`; the scheduler's task states describe tasks, not commits.
- Change data capture (`tickets`), the sign-up service and the scoring service write without the scheduler and are not
  in `_ops/`.

## Tables

### `customers`
`customer_id, signup_at, plan, postcode_district, last_login_at, _updated_at`: one row per customer.
- The sign-up service writes the row at `signup_at`: the plan chosen at sign-up (`basic`, `plus` or `family`), the
  postcode district, an empty `last_login_at`, and `_updated_at` = `signup_at`. `signup_at` and `postcode_district`
  never change.
- `crm_sync` reads the CRM at its start. For each customer whose plan or last login in the CRM (the latest login to
  the app or website before the sync's start) differs from the row, it overwrites `plan` and `last_login_at` with the
  CRM's values and sets `_updated_at` to the sync's commit time.
- Only plan changes are logged (`plan_changes`); no history of `last_login_at` is kept.

### `plan_changes`
`customer_id, changed_at, old_plan, new_plan, _loaded_at`: one row per plan change that `crm_sync` has applied. Each
sync writes one row for every change made in the CRM before its start that no earlier sync applied; `changed_at` is
when the customer made the change in the CRM, `_loaded_at` the commit of the sync that applied it. A customer's rows
are every change applied since sign-up, so the earliest row's `old_plan` is the plan chosen at sign-up. When one sync
applies several changes of a customer, the plan after that sync is the `new_plan` of the latest of them (by
`changed_at`), the CRM's plan at the sync's start.

### `scoring_points`
`customer_id, as_of, trigger, app_minutes_7d`: one row per scoring request, written by the scoring service at the
moment of the request, `as_of`. `trigger` is `batch` (the 06:00 run, which scores a customer every 14 days, on the
customer's billing weekday) or `ticket` (a request the support desk sends when a ticket is opened, for some of the
tickets, at the ticket's `opened_at`). `app_minutes_7d` is the product-analytics reading that came with the request (the customer's minutes in
the app over the last 7 days), empty when the request came without one (analytics export outages, devices offline).
`(customer_id, as_of)` is unique.

### `orders`
`order_id, customer_id, ordered_at, kind, amount_cents, _load_job, _loaded_at`. `kind` is `box` (the weekly box,
charged by billing at 05:30 on the customer's billing weekday; `ordered_at` is the charge) or `addon` (an extra item,
ordered at any time). Each order exists in the order system,

# Warehouse tables (churn scoring)

Written 2025-02-14 by the data platform for the warehouse and its nightly loaders as they were on that date, and not
updated since. The scheduler's own records of every job run and transaction, later changes included, are in each
extract's `_ops/` folder (below).

The seven tables below are the warehouse tables that the live scoring service (`live/features.py`) and the churn
pipeline (`churn/`) read. This page says what each table holds and which system writes it. Every brand of the company
runs the same warehouse and jobs; each brand's job runs, failures and changes are its own.

## Reading the warehouse
- A query that starts at a moment t sees exactly the rows and values committed before t: a row committed at or after
  t is not seen, and a value overwritten at or after t is seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of
  the event the row records.
- A query reads each table by the name it has when the query starts.
- `_loaded_at` is the commit time of the load that wrote the row; in `orders`, `_load_job` names that load.
- An extract is a copy of every table as the warehouse held it at one moment: the rows and values committed before
  that moment, with the `_ops/` records written before it.
- Timestamps are UTC, written as ISO 8601 with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds (`2025-02-04T06:00:00Z`);
  `snapshot_date` is a UTC date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); amounts are integer cents. Columns whose names start with `_` are
  written by the loaders, not by the source systems.

## The scheduler's records (`_ops/`)
- `_ops/scheduler.log` has one UTC event per line, `<time> <job> run=<run> <event>`: each task's start
  (`state=running`) and end (`state=success` or `state=failed`), and between them the lines the task writes, such as
  the rows it selected or copied, the transaction it sent (`sent txn <n> to commit`), the statements it ran and the
  checks it made.
- `_ops/commits.jsonl` has one JSON object per transaction a scheduled job sent: `txn`, `at`, `outcome` (`commit` or
  `rollback`), `table` and `rows` (the table the transaction writes rows into and how many; null for schema
  statements).
- `_ops/commits.jsonl` is the commit log of the scheduled jobs: a transaction is committed if and only if its outcome
  is `commit`, and it is committed at its `at`; the scheduler's task states describe tasks, not commits.
- Change data capture (`tickets`), the sign-up service and the scoring service write without the scheduler and are not
  in `_ops/`.

## Tables

### `customers`
`customer_id, signup_at, plan, postcode_district, last_login_at, _updated_at`: one row per customer.
- The sign-up service writes the row at `signup_at`: the plan chosen at sign-up (`basic`, `plus` or `family`), the
  postcode district, an empty `last_login_at`, and `_updated_at` = `signup_at`. `signup_at` and `postcode_district`
  never change.
- `crm_sync` reads the CRM at its start. For each customer whose plan or last login in the CRM (the latest login to
  the app or website before the sync's start) differs from the row, it overwrites `plan` and `last_login_at` with the
  CRM's values and sets `_updated_at` to the sync's commit time.
- Only plan changes are logged (`plan_changes`); no history of `last_login_at` is kept.

### `plan_changes`
`customer_id, changed_at, old_plan, new_plan, _loaded_at`: one row per plan change that `crm_sync` has applied. Each
sync writes one row for every change made in the CRM before its start that no earlier sync applied; `changed_at` is
when the customer made the change in the CRM, `_loaded_at` the commit of the sync that applied it. A customer's rows
are every change applied since sign-up, so the earliest row's `old_plan` is the plan chosen at sign-up. When one sync
applies several changes of a customer, the plan after that sync is the `new_plan` of the latest of them (by
`changed_at`), the CRM's plan at the sync's start.

### `scoring_points`
`customer_id, as_of, trigger, app_minutes_7d`: one row per scoring request, written by the scoring service at the
moment of the request, `as_of`. `trigger` is `batch` (the 06:00 run, which scores a customer every 14 days, on the
customer's billing weekday) or `ticket` (a request the support desk sends when a ticket is opened, for some of the
tickets, at the ticket's `opened_at`). `app_minutes_7d` is the product-analytics reading that came with the request (the customer's minutes in
the app over the last 7 days), empty when the request came without one (analytics export outages, devices offline).
`(customer_id, as_of)` is unique.

### `orders`
`order_id, customer_id, ordered_at, kind, amount_cents, _load_job, _loaded_at`. `kind` is `box` (the weekly box,
charged by billing at 05:30 on the customer's billing weekday; `ordered_at` is the charge) or `addon` (an extra item,
ordered at any time). Each order exists in the order system,

"""Account status from the billing system's status snapshots, point in time (INC-2041).

A snapshot dated D records the status at the end of day D, so a prediction at t may only use snapshots dated before
date(t).
"""
import pandas as pd


def latest_status(points, snapshots):
    """Status of the customer's latest snapshot dated before the prediction's UTC date (null if none)."""
    left = points[["customer_id"]].assign(day=points["as_of"].dt.floor("D")).reset_index()
    left = left.sort_values("day", kind="mergesort")
    snaps = snapshots.sort_values("snapshot_date", kind="mergesort")[["customer_id", "snapshot_date", "status"]]
    snaps = snaps.assign(snapshot_date=snaps["snapshot_date"].astype(left["day"].dtype))
    m = pd.merge_asof(left, snaps, left_on="day", right_on="snapshot_date", by="customer_id",
                      allow_exact_matches=False)
    return m.set_index("index")["status"].reindex(points.index)

"""Gap filling for upstream readings that arrive with holes (analytics export outages, devices offline).

Point in time (INC-2041): a missing reading takes the customer's most recent earlier reading, never a later one; with
no earlier reading it stays null.
"""


def fill_app_minutes(points):
    """Fill missing app_minutes_7d from the same customer's last earlier reading."""
    pts = points.sort_values(["customer_id", "as_of"], kind="mergesort")
    filled = pts.groupby("customer_id")["app_minutes_7d"].ffill()
    return filled.reindex(points.index)

"""Customer attributes from the customer record (new in v3): the subscription plan and the days since the last login.

Point in time: a last login at or after the prediction time is ignored (the feature is null then), so the feature
never looks ahead of t.
"""


def plan(points, customers):
    """The customer's subscription plan."""
    return points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["plan"])


def days_since_last_login(points, customers):
    """t minus the customer's last login, in days; null when the record has no login before t."""
    last = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["last_login_at"])

"""Target encoding of high-cardinality categoricals, point in time (INC-2041).

A label row records whether the customer churned in the 30 days after its own prediction, so its outcome is final only
once that window has closed (as_of + 30 days). A prediction at t uses only labels whose window closed before t, for the
district counts and for the prior alike; its own label and every later one are never seen.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

PRIOR_WEIGHT = 20
DEFAULT_PRIOR = 0.05
LABEL_WINDOW_DAYS = 30
EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def district_encoding(points, labels, customers, m=PRIOR_WEIGHT):
    """Smoothed churn rate of the customer's postcode district, from labels whose window closed before t."""
    district = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab_d = labels["customer_id"].map(district)
    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(district)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(pd.concat([lab_d, pt_d], ignore_index=True))
    lab_code, pt_code = codes[:len(labels)].astype("int64"), codes[len(labels):].astype("int64")
    closed = _seconds(labels["as_of"]) + LABEL_WINDOW_DAYS * 86400
    y = labels["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])

    order = np.argsort(closed, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(closed[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), DEFAULT_PRIOR)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    key = lab_code * STRIDE + closed
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    n, s = hi - lo, ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return pd.Series((s + m * prior) / (n + m), index=points.index, dtype="float64")

"""Load a warehouse extract (the seven CSV files described in docs/WAREHOUSE.md) into pandas frames.

Every timestamp column is parsed to a UTC timestamp, the load metadata columns included, so each frame carries
everything its CSV file has.
"""
import os
import pandas as pd

TIMESTAMPS = {
    "customers": ["signup_at", "last_login_at", "_updated_at"],
    "plan_changes": ["changed_at", "_loaded_at"],
    "scoring_points": ["as_of"],
    "orders": ["ordered_at", "_loaded_at"],
    "tickets": ["opened_at", "_loaded_at"],
    "status_snapshots": ["snapshot_date", "_loaded_at"],
    "labels": ["as_of", "_loaded_at"],
}


def load_extract(data_dir):
    tables = {}
    for name, cols in TIMESTAMPS.items():
        df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{name}.csv"), dtype={"postcode_district": "str"})
        for c in cols:
            df[c] = pd.to_datetime(df[c], utc=True)
        tables[name] = df
    tables["scoring_points"]["app_minutes_7d"] = tables["scoring_points"]["app_minutes_7d"].astype("float64")
    return tables

"""Activity features over trailing windows (orders, spend, tickets) and simple time-since features.

Point in time (INC-2041): a window is [t - W days, t) on the exact event timestamps, so an event stamped at or after
the prediction time is never counted and nothing later in the day leaks in.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10  # composite key customer_id * STRIDE + epoch seconds (seconds stay below 1e10 until 2286)


def _seconds(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _window(points, events, ts_col, days, amount_col=None):
    """Per prediction: number (and amount sum) of the customer's events with t - days <= ts < t."""
    ev_key = events["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + _seconds(events[ts_col])
    order = np.argsort(ev_key, kind="stable")
    ev_key = ev_key[order]
    cid = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE
    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    hi = np.searchsorted(ev_key, cid + t, side="left")
    lo = np.searchsorted(ev_key, cid + t - days * 86400, side="left")
    count = hi - lo
    if amount_col is None:
        return count, None
    pref = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(events[amount_col].to_numpy(dtype="int64")[order])])
    return count, pref[hi] - pref[lo]


def activity_features(points, orders, tickets):
    out = points[["customer_id", "as_of"]].copy()
    out["orders_7d"], _ = _window(points, orders, "ordered_at", 7)
    out["orders_30d"], out["spend_30d_cents"] = _window(points, orders, "ordered_at", 30, "amount_cents")
    out["tickets_30d"], _ = _window(points, tickets, "opened_at", 30)

    # time since the last order strictly before the prediction
    o = orders.sort_values("ordered_at")[["customer_id", "ordered_at"]]
    left = out[["customer_id", "as_of"]].reset_index().sort_values("as_of")
    last = pd.merge_asof(left, o, left_on="as_of", right_on="ordered_at", by="customer_id",
                         allow_exact_matches=False).set_index("index").sort_index()["ordered_at"]
    out["days_since_last_order"] = (out["as_of"] - last).dt.total_seconds() / 86400
    return out


def tenure_days(points, customers):
    signup = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["signup_at"])
    return (points["as_of"] - signup).dt.total_seconds() / 86400

import pandas as pd, json

"""Parse the warehouse scheduler records needed for point-in-time reconstruction."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
import json
import os
import re

import pandas as pd


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OrderTxn:
    start: pd.Timestamp
    end: pd.Timestamp
    rows: int
    commit: pd.Timestamp
    table: str
    txn: int


@dataclass
class Ops:
    order_txns: list
    schema_txns: list
    rename_at: pd.Timestamp | None = None


_SELECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"selected\s+orders\s+where\s+ordered_at\s*>=\s*(\S+)\s+"
    r"and\s+ordered_at\s*<\s*(\S+):\s*(\d+)\s+rows;\s*"
    r"sent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?"
)
_STATEMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^statement:\s*(.*)$")
_SEND_RE = re.compile(r"\bsent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?")
_RENAME_RE = re.compile(r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\S+)\s+RENAME\s+TO\s+(\S+)", re.I)


def _utc(value):
    return pd.to_datetime(value, utc=True)


def _table_name(value):
    return value.strip('"`').split(".")[-1]


def load_ops(data_dir):
    commits = {}
    path = os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "commits.jsonl")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                row = json.loads(line)
                commits[int(row["txn"])] = {
                    "at": _utc(row["at"]),
                    "outcome": row.get("outcome"),
                    "table": row.get("table"),
                    "rows": row.get("rows"),
                }

    order_txns = []
    schema_txns = []
    statements = []
    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split(maxsplit=2)
            if len(parts) != 3:
                continue
            message = parts[2]

            if message.startswith("state=running"):
                statements = []
                continue

            match = _STATEMENT_RE.match(message)
            if match:
                statements.append(match.group(1))
                continue

            match = _SELECT_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                start_s, end_s, rows, txn_s, table = match.groups()
                txn = int(txn_s)
                commit = commits.get(txn, {}).get("at")
                if commits.get(txn, {}).get("outcome") == "commit" and commit is not None:
                    order_txns.append(OrderTxn(
                        _utc(start_s), _utc(end_s), int(rows), commit,
                        _table_name(table or "orders"), txn,
                    ))
                statements = []
                continue

            match = _SEND_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                txn = int(match.group(1))
                if commits.get(txn, {}).get("outcome") == "commit" and statements:
                    schema_txns.append({
                        "txn": txn,
                        "at": commits[txn]["at"],
                        "statements": tuple(statements),
                    })
                statements = []

    rename_at = None
    for txn in schema_txns:
        renames = [_RENAME_RE.fullmatch(statement) for statement in txn["statements"]]
        renames = [( _table_name(a), _table_name(b)) for a, b in
                   (match.groups() for match in renames if match)]
        moved_old = any(a == "orders" and b != "orders" for a, b in renames)
        installed_new = any(a == "orders_new" and b == "orders" for a, b in renames)
        if moved_old and installed_new:
            rename_at = txn["at"] if rename_at is None else min(rename_at, txn["at"])

    return Ops(order_txns=order_txns, schema_txns=schema_txns, rename_at=rename_at)


def assign_legacy_order_commits(orders, ops, rename_at):
    """Map source orders to their commits into the old generation named *orders*.

    A failed/rolled-back load is retried with an expanding ordered_at interval.  For
    each source order, the earliest successful transaction whose interval contains
    its timestamp is therefore the transaction that first committed it.
    """
    commits = pd.Series(pd.NaT, index=orders.index, dtype="datetime64[ns, UTC]")
    if rename_at is None:
        orders["_legacy_commit"] = commits
        return

    records = [x for x in ops.order_txns
               if x.table == "orders" and x.commit < rename_at]
    if not records:
        orders["_legacy_commit"] = commits
        return

    records.sort(key=lambda x: x.start)
    starts, valid = _seconds(pd.Series([x.start for x in records]))
    ends, _ = _seconds(pd.Series([x.end for x in records]))
    commit_secs, _ = _seconds(pd.Series([x.commit for x in records]))

    event_times, event_valid = _seconds(orders["ordered_at"])
    unique, inverse = np.unique(event_times[event_valid], return_inverse=True)
    assigned = np.full(len(unique), -1, dtype="int64")
    active = []
    pos = 0
    for event_no, ts in enumerate(unique):
        while pos < len(records) and starts[pos] <= ts:
            heapq.heappush(active, (int(commit_secs[pos]), int(ends[pos]), pos))
            pos += 1
        while active and active[0][1] <= ts:
            heapq.heappop(active)
        if active:
            assigned[event_no] = active[0][2]

    out = np.full(len(orders), np.iinfo(np.int64).min, dtype="int64")
    positions = np.flatnonzero(event_valid)
    vals = assigned[inverse]
    hit = vals >= 0
    out[positions[hit]] = commit_secs[vals[hit]]
    result = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(out, index=orders.index), unit="s", utc=True)
    orders["_legacy_commit"] = result.where(out != np.iinfo(np.int64).min, pd.NaT)

"""Read the warehouse scheduler records used for point-in-time reconstruction."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
import heapq
import json
import os
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OrderTxn:
    start: pd.Timestamp
    end: pd.Timestamp
    rows: int
    commit: pd.Timestamp
    table: str
    txn: int


@dataclass
class Ops:
    order_txns: list
    schema_txns: list
    rename_at: pd.Timestamp | None = None
    legacy_orders_complete: bool = True


_SELECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"selected\s+orders\s+where\s+ordered_at\s*>=\s*(\S+)\s+"
    r"and\s+ordered_at\s*<\s*(\S+):\s*(\d+)\s+rows;\s*"
    r"sent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?"
)
_STATEMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^statement:\s*(.*)$")
_SEND_RE = re.compile(r"\bsent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?")
_RENAME_RE = re.compile(r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\S+)\s+RENAME\s+TO\s+(\S+)", re.I)


def _utc(value):
    return pd.to_datetime(value, utc=True)


def _table_name(value):
    return value.strip('"`').split(".")[-1]


def load_ops(data_dir):
    commits = {}
    path = os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "commits.jsonl")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                if line.strip():
                    row = json.loads(line)
                    commits[int(row["txn"])] = {
                        "at": _utc(row["at"]),
                        "outcome": row.get("outcome"),
                        "table": row.get("table"),
                        "rows": row.get("rows"),
                    }

    order_txns = []
    schema_txns = []
    statements = {}
    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split(maxsplit=2)
            if len(parts) != 3:
                continue
            job, message = parts[1], parts[2]

            if message.startswith("state=running"):
                statements[job] = []
                continue

            match = _STATEMENT_RE.match(message)
            if match:
                statements.setdefault(job, []).append(match.group(1))
                continue

            match = _SELECT_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                start_s, end_s, rows, txn_s, table = match.groups()
                txn = int(txn_s)
                info = commits.get(txn, {})
                if info.get("outcome") == "commit" and info.get("at") is not None:
                    order_txns.append(OrderTxn(
                        _utc(start_s), _utc(end_s), int(rows), info["at"],
                        _table_name(table or "orders"), txn,
                    ))
                statements[job] = []
                continue

            match = _SEND_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                txn = int(match.group(1))
                info = commits.get(txn, {})
                if info.get("outcome") == "commit" and info.get("at") is not None and statements.get(job):
                    schema_txns.append({
                        "txn": txn,
                        "at": info["at"],
                        "statements": tuple(statements[job]),
                    })
                statements[job] = []

    schema_txns.sort(key=lambda x: x["at"])
    names = {"orders": "orders"}
    current_identity = names["orders"]
    rename_at = None
    for txn in schema_txns:
        for statement in txn["statements"]:
            match = _RENAME_RE.fullmatch(statement)
            if not match:
                continue
            old_name, new_name = map(_table_name, match.groups())
            names[new_name] = names.get(old_name, old_name)
            if old_name != new_name:
                names.pop(old_name, None)
        if names.get("orders") != current_identity:
            if rename_at is None:
                rename_at = txn["at"]
            current_identity = names.get("orders")

    return Ops(order_txns=order_txns, schema_txns=schema_txns, rename_at=rename_at)


def _seconds(values):
    values = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(values), utc=True)
    valid = values.notna().to_numpy()
    out = values.to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]").astype("int64") // 1_000_000_000
    return out, valid


def assign_legacy_order_commits(orders, ops, rename_at):
    """Assign old-generation commit times to orders from scheduler intervals.

    After a failed load the next legacy load uses an expanding ordered_at interval.
    Thus the earliest successful transaction containing an order's timestamp is the
    transaction that first committed it to the old ``orders`` generation.
    """
    orders["_legacy_commit"] = pd.NaT
    ops.legacy_orders_complete = True
    if rename_at is None:
        return

    records = [x for x in ops.order_txns
               if x.table == "orders" and x.commit < rename_at]
    if not records:
        return
    records.sort(key=lambda x: (x.start, x.commit, x.txn))

    starts, _ = _seconds([x.start for x in records])
    ends, _ = _seconds([x.end for x in records])
    commit_secs, _ = _seconds([x.commit for x in records])
    event_secs, event_valid = _seconds(orders["ordered_at"])
    if event_valid.any():
        unique, inverse, counts = np.unique(event_secs[event_valid], return_inverse=True,
                                            return_counts=True)
        assigned = np.full(len(unique), -1, dtype="int64")
        active = []
        pos = 0
        for event_no, ts in enumerate(unique):
            while pos < len(records) and starts[pos] <= ts:
                heapq.heappush(active, (int(commit_secs[pos]), int(ends[pos]), pos))
                pos += 1
            while active and active[0][1] <= ts:
                heapq.heappop(active)
            if active:
                assigned[event_no] = active[0][2]

        txn_counts = np.zeros(len(records), dtype="int64")
        hit = assigned >= 0
        if hit.any():
            np.add.at(txn_counts, assigned[hit], counts[hit])
        expected = np.asarray([x.rows for x in records], dtype="int64")
        ops.legacy_orders_complete = bool(np.array_equal(txn_counts, expected))

        out = np.full(len(orders), np.iinfo(np.int64).min, dtype="int64")
        positions = np.flatnonzero(event_valid)
        vals = assigned[inverse]
        good = vals >= 0
        out[positions[good]] = commit_secs[vals[good]]
        result = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(out, index=orders.index), unit="s", utc=True)
        orders["_legacy_commit"] = result.where(out != np.iinfo(np.int64).min, pd.NaT)

"""Reconstruct the values computed by ``live/features.py`` from an extract.

The reconstruction uses only facts that were committed before each request.  For
rows written by scheduled jobs this comes from ``_loaded_at`` (or, for the old
orders generation, from the scheduler transaction records).  Rows written by the
sign-up, ticket CDC and scoring services were committed at the source timestamps
recorded in the extract.
"""
from bisect import bisect_left, insort

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def _seconds(values):
    values = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(values), utc=True)
    valid = values.notna().to_numpy()
    out = values.to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]").astype("int64") // 1_000_000_000
    return out, valid


class _Fenwick:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.counts = [0] * (n + 1)
        self.amounts = [0] * (n + 1)

    def add(self, i, amount):
        i += 1
        while i <= self.n:
            self.counts[i] += 1
            self.amounts[i] += amount
            i += i & -i

    def range(self, left, right):
        if right <= left:
            return 0, 0
        return self._prefix(right) - self._prefix(left)

    def _prefix(self, i):
        count = amount = 0
        while i > 0:
            count += self.counts[i]
            amount += self.amounts[i]
            i -= i & -i
        return count, amount


def _factorize_ids(a, b=None):
    if b is None:
        codes, unique = pd.factorize(pd.Series(a), sort=True)
        return codes, unique
    combined = pd.concat([pd.Series(a), pd.Series(b)], ignore_index=True)
    codes, unique = pd.factorize(combined, sort=True)
    return codes[: len(a)], codes[len(a) :], unique


def _event_features(points, events, commit_col, ts_col, *, amount_col=None,
                    windows=(30,), need_last=False):
    """Evaluate event queries as events become visible through ``commit_col``."""
    n = len(points)
    result = {f"count_{w}": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64") for w in windows}
    if amount_col is not None:
        result["spend"] = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    result["last"] = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")

    point_secs, point_valid = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    point_positions = np.flatnonzero(point_valid)
    if not len(point_positions):
        return result
    point_secs = point_secs[point_positions]

    event_secs, event_valid = _seconds(events[ts_col])
    event_commit, commit_valid = _seconds(events[commit_col])
    event_mask = event_valid & commit_valid
    event_positions = np.flatnonzero(event_mask)
    event_secs = event_secs[event_positions]
    event_commit = event_commit[event_positions]

    if len(events):
        point_codes, event_codes, _ = _factorize_ids(
            points["customer_id"].iloc[point_positions],
            events["customer_id"].iloc[event_positions],
        )
    else:
        point_codes, _ = _factorize_ids(points["customer_id"].iloc[point_positions])
        event_codes = np.empty(0, dtype="int64")

    all_secs = np.concatenate([point_secs, event_secs]) if len(event_secs) else point_secs
    base = int(all_secs.min())
    span = int(all_secs.max()) - base + 1

    point_keys = point_codes.astype("int64") * span + (point_secs - base)
    if len(event_secs):
        event_keys = event_codes.astype("int64") * span + (event_secs - base)
        sorted_index = np.argsort(event_keys, kind="mergesort")
        event_keys = event_keys[sorted_index]
        ranks = np.empty(len(event_keys), dtype="int64")
        ranks[sorted_index] = np.arange(len(event_keys), dtype="int64")
    else:
        event_keys = np.empty(0, dtype="int64")
        ranks = np.empty(0, dtype="int64")

    if amount_col is not None and len(event_positions):
        amounts = pd.to_numeric(events[amount_col].iloc[event_positions],
                                errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype("int64").to_numpy()
    else:
        amounts = np.zeros(len(event_positions), dtype="int64")

    tree = _Fenwick(len(event_keys))
    event_order = np.argsort(event_commit, kind="mergesort")
    event_commit = event_commit[event_order]
    event_order = event_positions[event_order]
    ranks = ranks[event_order]
    event_secs = event_secs[event_order]
    event_codes = event_codes[event_order]
    amounts = amounts[event_order]

    histories = [[] for _ in range(len(point_codes))] if need_last else None
    event_pos = 0
    for q, original in enumerate(point_positions):
        t = int(point_secs[q])
        code = int(point_codes[q])
        while event_pos < len(event_order) and event_commit[event_pos] < t:
            i = int(event_order[event_pos])
            tree.add(int(ranks[event_pos]), int(amounts[event_pos]))
            if histories is not None:
                insort(histories[code], int(event_secs[event_pos]))
            event_pos += 1

        for window in windows:
            lower_adj = max(t - int(window) * 86400 - base, 0)
            upper_adj = max(t - base, 0)
            left = bisect_left(event_keys, code * span + lower_adj)
            right = bisect_left(event_keys, code * span + upper_adj)
            count, _ = tree.range(left, right)
            result[f"count_{window}"][original] = count

        if amount_col is not None:
            lower_adj = max(t - 30 * 86400 - base, 0)
            upper_adj = max(t - base, 0)
            left = bisect_left(event_keys, code * span + lower_adj)
            right = bisect_left(event_keys, code * span + upper_adj)
            result["spend"][original] = tree.range(left, right)[1]

        if histories is not None:
            hist = histories[code]
            hi = bisect_left(hist, t)
            if hi:
                result["last"][original] = float(hist[hi - 1] - t) / 86400.0

    return result


def order_features(points, orders, rename_at, legacy_orders_complete):
    """Live order features across the old and new physical orders tables."""
    n = len(points)
    out = {
        "orders_7d": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "orders_30d": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "spend_30d_cents": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "days_since_last_order": np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64"),
    }
    known = bool(orders["_loaded_at"].notna().all() and legacy_orders_complete)

    if rename_at is None:
        values = _event_features(
            points, orders, "_loaded_at", "ordered_at",
            amount_col="amount_cents", windows=(7, 30), need_last=True,
        )
        for name in out:
            out[name] = values["spend"] if name == "spend_30d_cents" else values.get(name, values["last"])
        return out, known

    old_mask = (points["as_of"] <= rename_at).to_numpy()
    new_mask = ~old_mask
    old_points = points.loc[old_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
    new_points = points.loc[new_mask].reset_index(drop=True)

    if old_mask.any():
        old_events = orders.loc[orders["_legacy_commit"].notna()].copy()
        values = _event_features(
            old_points, old_events, "_legacy_commit", "ordered_at",
            amount_col="amount_cents", windows=(7, 30), need_last=True,
        )
        out["orders_7d"][old_mask] = values["count_7"]
        out["orders_30d"][old_mask] = values["count_30"]
        out["spend_30d_cents"][old_mask] = values["spend"]
        out["days_since_last_order"][old_mask] = values["last"]

    if new_mask.any():
        new_events = orders.loc[orders["_loaded_at"].notna()].copy()
        values = _event_features(
            new_points, new_events, "_loaded_at", "ordered_at",
            amount_col="amount_cents", windows=(7, 30), need_last=True,
        )
        out["orders_7d"][new_mask] = values["count_7"]
        out["orders_30d"][new_mask] = values["count_30"]
        out["spend_30d_cents"][new_mask] = values["spend"]
        out["days_since_last_order"][new_mask] = values["last"]
    return out, known


def ticket_features(points, tickets):
    values = _event_features(
        points, tickets, "_loaded_at", "opened_at", windows=(30,), need_last=False,
    )
    return values["count_30"]


def status_features(points, snapshots):
    n = len(points)
    out = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)
    point_secs, point_valid = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    point_positions = np.flatnonzero(point_valid)
    if not len(point_positions):
        return out

    snap_secs, snap_valid = _seconds(snapshots["_loaded_at"])
    snap_dates, date_valid = _seconds(snapshots["snapshot_date"])
    snap_mask = snap_valid & date_valid
    snap_positions = np.flatnonzero(snap_mask)
    snap_secs = snap_secs[snap_positions]
    snap_dates = snap_dates[snap_positions]
    statuses = snapshots["status"].to_numpy(dtype=object)[snap_positions]

    point_codes, snap_codes, _ = _factorize_ids(
        points["customer_id"].iloc[point_positions],
        snapshots["customer_id"].iloc[snap_positions],
    )
    point_codes = np.asarray(point_codes, dtype="int64")
    snap_codes = np.asarray(snap_codes, dtype="int64")
    snap_order = np.argsort(snap_secs, kind="mergesort")
    snap_secs = snap_secs[snap_order]
    snap_dates = snap_dates[snap_order]
    statuses = statuses[snap_order]
    snap_codes = snap_codes[snap_order]

    latest = {}
    snap_i = 0
    for q, original in enumerate(point_positions):
        t = int(point_secs[q])
        while snap_i < len(snap_secs) and snap_secs[snap_i] < t:
            code = int(snap_codes[snap_i])
            date = int(snap_dates[snap_i])
            if code not in latest or date > latest[code][0]:
                latest[code] = (date, statuses[snap_i])
            snap_i += 1
        current = latest.get(int(point_codes[q]))
        if current is not None:
            out[original] = current[1]
    return out


def target_encoding(points, labels, customers):
    n = len(points)
    out = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    point_secs, point_valid = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    point_positions = np.flatnonzero(point_valid)
    if not len(point_positions):
        return out
    point_secs = point_secs[point_positions]

    customer_ids = customers["customer_id"]
    signup = customers["signup_at"]
    district = customers["postcode_district"].astype("object")
    lab_ids = labels["customer_id"]
    point_ids = points["customer_id"].iloc[point_positions]
    all_ids = pd.concat([lab_ids, point_ids], ignore_index=True)
    codes, unique = pd.factorize(all_ids, sort=True)
    lab_codes = np.asarray(codes[: len(labels)], dtype="int64")
    point_codes = np.asarray(codes[len(labels) :], dtype="int64")
    unique_ids = np.asarray(unique, dtype="int64")
    id_to_customer = pd.Series(np.arange(len(customers), dtype="int64"), index=customer_ids)
    customer_index = id_to_customer.reindex(unique_ids).to_numpy(dtype="float64")

    customer_index = np.where(has_customer, customer_index, 0).astype("int64")

    lab_district = district.iloc[np.where(has_customer[: len(labels)], customer_index[: len(labels)], 0)].to_numpy(dtype=object)
    lab_district = np.where(has_customer[: len(labels)], lab_district, None)
    pt_district = district.iloc[np.where(has_customer[len(labels):], customer_index[len(labels):], 0)].to_numpy(dtype=object)
    pt_district = np.where(has_customer[len(labels):], pt_district, None)

    district_values = pd.concat([
        pd.Series(lab_district, dtype="object"),
        pd.Series(pt_district, dtype="object"),
    ], ignore_index=True)
    district_codes, _ = pd.factorize(district_values, use_na_sentinel=True)
    lab_district = np.asarray(district_codes[: len(labels)], dtype="int64")
    pt_district = np.asarray(district_codes[len(labels):], dtype="int64")
    pt_district = np.where(pt_district >= 0, pt_district, -999999)

    lab_commit, lab_commit_valid = _seconds(labels["_loaded_at"])
    lab_signup_secs = np.full(len(labels), np.iinfo(np.int64).max, dtype="int64")
    visible_customer = has_customer[: len(labels)]
    if visible_customer.any():

    y_values = y_values[label_order]

    district_n = {}
    district_sum = {}
    label_i = 0

        t = int(point_secs[q])
        code = int(point_codes[q])
        own = int(pt_district[q])

            y = float(y_values[label_i]) if np.isfinite(y_values[label_i]) else np.nan
            if np.isfinite(y):

                global_sum += int(y)
            district = int(lab_district[label_i])
            district_n[district] = district_n.get(district, 0) + 1
            district_sum[district] = district_sum.get(district, 0) + (int(y) if np.isfinite(y) else 0)

        prior = global_sum / global_n if global_n else 0.05

def build(data_dir):
    tables = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = tables["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    customers = tables["customers"]
    orders = tables["orders"].copy()
    tickets = tables["tickets"]
    snapshots = tables["status_snapshots"]
    labels = tables["labels"]
    plan_changes = tables["plan_changes"]

    ops = load_ops(data_dir)
    assign_legacy_order_commits(orders, ops, ops.rename_at)

    out = points[["customer_id", "as_of"]].copy()
    values, orders_known = order_features(
        points, orders, ops.rename_at, ops.legacy_orders_complete,
    )
    if orders_known:
        out["orders_7d"] = values["orders_7d"]
        out["orders_30d"] = values["orders_30d"]
        out["spend_30d_cents"] = values["spend_30d_cents"]
        out["days_since_last_order"] = values["days_since_last_order"]

    out["tickets_30d"] = ticket_features(points, tickets)

    signup = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["signup_at"])
    tenure = (points["as_of"] - signup).dt.total_seconds() / 86400.0
    exists = signup.notna() & (signup < points["as_of"])
    out["tenure_days"] = tenure.where(exists)

    out["status"] = status_features(points, snapshots)
    plan, login, keep_plan, keep_login = customer_features(points, customers, plan_changes)
    if keep_plan:
        out["plan"] = plan
    if keep_login:
        out["days_since_last_login"] = login
    out["app_minutes_7d"] = app_minutes(points)
    out["te_district"] = target_encoding(points, labels, customers)

    kept = [f for f in LIVE_FEATURES if f in out.columns]
    return out[BASE_COLUMNS + kept]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    features = build(args.data)
    out_path = os.path.abspath(args.out)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path), exist_ok=True)
    features.to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(features)} rows x {features.shape[1]} columns to {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def order_features(points, orders, rename_at, legacy_orders_complete):
    """Live order features across the old and new physical orders tables."""
    n = len(points)
    out = {
        "orders_7d": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "orders_30d": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "spend_30d_cents": np.zeros(n, dtype="int64"),
        "days_since_last_order": np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64"),
    }
    known = bool(orders["_loaded_at"].notna().all() and legacy_orders_complete)

    if rename_at is None:
        values = _event_features(
            points, orders, "_loaded_at", "ordered_at",
            amount_col="amount_cents", windows=(7, 30), need_last=True,
        )
        for name in out:
            out[name] = values["spend"] if name == "spend_30d_cents" else values.get(name, values["last"])
        return out, known

    old_mask = (points["as_of"] <= rename_at).to_numpy()
    new_mask = ~old_mask
    old_points = points.loc[old_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
    new_points = points.loc[new_mask].reset_index(drop=True)

    if old_mask.any():
        old_events = orders.loc[orders["_legacy_commit"].notna()].copy()
        values = _event_features(
            old_points, old_events, "_legacy_commit", "ordered_at",
            amount_col="amount_cents", windows=(7, 30), need_last=True,
        )
        out["orders_7d"][old_mask] = values["count_7"]
        out["orders_30d"][old_mask] = values["count_30"]

"""Read warehouse scheduler records needed for point-in-time reconstruction."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
import heapq
import json
import os
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OrderTxn:
    start: pd.Timestamp
    end: pd.Timestamp
    rows: int
    commit: pd.Timestamp
    table: str
    txn: int


@dataclass
class Ops:
    order_txns: list
    schema_txns: list
    rename_at: pd.Timestamp | None = None
    legacy_orders_complete: bool = True


_SELECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"selected\s+orders\s+where\s+ordered_at\s*>=\s*(\S+)\s+"
    r"and\s+ordered_at\s*<\s*(\S+):\s*(\d+)\s+rows;\s*"
    r"sent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?"
)
_SEND_RE = re.compile(r"\bsent\s+txn\s+(\d+)\s+to\s+commit(?:\s+into\s+(\S+))?")
_RENAME_RE = re.compile(r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\S+)\s+RENAME\s+TO\s+(\S+)", re.I)


def _utc(value):
    return pd.to_datetime(value, utc=True)


def _table_name(value):
    return value.strip('"`').split(".")[-1]


def load_ops(data_dir):
    commits = {}
    path = os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "commits.jsonl")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                if line.strip():
                    row = json.loads(line)
                    commits[int(row["txn"])] = {
                        "at": _utc(row["at"]),
                        "outcome": row.get("outcome"),
                        "table": row.get("table"),
                        "rows": row.get("rows"),
                    }

    order_txns = []
    schema_txns = []
    statements = {}
    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, "_ops", "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split(maxsplit=2)
            if len(parts) != 3:
                continue
            job, message = parts[1], parts[2]

            if "state=running" in message:
                statements[job] = []
                continue
            if "state=" in message:
                statements[job] = []
                continue

            if "statement:" in message:
                statement = message.split("statement:", 1)[1].strip()
                statements.setdefault(job, []).append(statement)
                continue

            match = _SELECT_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                start_s, end_s, rows, txn_s, table = match.groups()
                txn = int(txn_s)
                info = commits.get(txn, {})
                if info.get("outcome") == "commit" and info.get("at") is not None:
                    order_txns.append(OrderTxn(
                        _utc(start_s), _utc(end_s), int(rows), info["at"],
                        _table_name(table or "orders"), txn,
                    ))
                statements[job] = []
                continue

            match = _SEND_RE.search(message)
            if match:
                txn = int(match.group(1))
                info = commits.get(txn, {})
                if info.get("outcome") == "commit" and info.get("at") is not None and statements.get(job):
                    schema_txns.append({
                        "txn": txn,
                        "at": info["at"],
                        "statements": tuple(statements[job]),
                    })
                statements[job] = []

    schema_txns.sort(key=lambda x: x["at"])
    rename_at = None
    identities = {"orders": "orders-initial"}
    for txn in schema_txns:
        before = identities.get("orders")
        for statement in txn["statements"]:
            match = _RENAME_RE.fullmatch(statement)
            if not match:
                continue
            old_name, new_name = map(_table_name, match.groups())
            identity = identities.pop(old_name, old_name)
            identities[new_name] = identity
        after = identities.get("orders")
        if after != before and rename_at is None:
            rename_at = txn["at"]

    return Ops(order_txns=order_txns, schema_txns=schema_txns, rename_at=rename_at)


def _seconds(values):
    values = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(values), utc=True)
    valid = values.notna().to_numpy()
    out = values.to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]").astype("int64") // 1_000_000_000
    return out, valid


def assign_legacy_order_commits(orders, ops, rename_at):
    """Assign old-generation commit times to orders from scheduler intervals.

    A rolled-back legacy load is retried with an expanding ordered_at interval, so
    the earliest successful transaction containing an order timestamp is the load
    that first committed it to the old ``orders`` table.  Exact transaction counts
    are checked before the result is considered complete.
    """
    orders["_legacy_commit"] = pd.NaT
    ops.legacy_orders_complete = True
    if rename_at is None:
        return

    records = [x for x in ops.order_txns
               if x.table == "orders" and x.commit < rename_at]
    if not records:
        return
    records.sort(key=lambda x: (x.start, x.commit, x.txn))

    starts, _ = _seconds([x.start for x in records])
    ends, _ = _seconds([x.end for x in records])
    commit_secs, _ = _seconds([x.commit for x in records])
    event_secs, event_valid = _seconds(orders["ordered_at"])
    if event_valid.any():
        unique, inverse, counts = np.unique(event_secs[event_valid],
                                            return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
        assigned = np.full(len(unique), -1, dtype="int64")
        active = []
        pos = 0
        for event_no, ts in enumerate(unique):
            while pos < len(records) and starts[pos] <= ts:
                heapq.heappush(active, (int(commit_secs[pos]), int(ends[pos]), pos))
                pos += 1
            while active and active[0][1] <= ts:
                heapq.heappop(active)
            if active:
                assigned[event_no] = active[0][2]

        txn_counts = np.zeros(len(records), dtype="int64")
        hit = assigned >= 0
        if hit.any():
            np.add.at(txn_counts, assigned[hit], counts[hit])
        expected = np.asarray([x.rows for x in records], dtype="int64")
        ops.legacy_orders_complete = bool(np.array_equal(txn_counts, expected))

        out = np.full(len(orders), np.iinfo(np.int64).min, dtype="int64")
        positions = np.flatnonzero(event_valid)
        vals = assigned[inverse]
        good = vals >= 0
        out[positions[good]] = commit_secs[vals[good]]
        result = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(out, index=orders.index), unit="s", utc=True)
        orders["_legacy_commit"] = result.where(out != np.iinfo(np.int64).min, pd.NaT)

import json,pandas as pd
O=pd.read_parquet('/tmp/fixed2.parquet')
L=pd.DataFrame([{'customer_id':x['customer_id'],'as_of':x['as_of'],**x['features']} for x in map(json.loads,open('logs/live_2026-01_sample.jsonl'))])
L['as_of']=pd.to_datetime(L.as_of,utc=True)
M=L.merge(O,on=['customer_id','as_of'],how='left',suffixes=('_live','_off'))
print('shape',O.shape,'columns',list(O.columns),'unmatched',int(M['orders_7d_off'].isna().sum()))
for f in ['orders_7d','orders_30d','spend_30d_cents','tickets_30d','days_since_last_order','tenure_days','status','plan','days_since_last_login','app_minutes_7d','te_district']:
    if f not in O:
        print(f,'omitted')
        continue
    a=M[f+'_live']; b=M[f+'_off']
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(a) and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(b):
        bad=~(((a-b).abs()<=1e-6+1e-9*a.abs())|(a.isna()&b.isna()))
    else:
        bad=~((a==b)|(a.isna()&b.isna()))
    print(f,'mismatches',int(bad.sum()),'/',len(M),'off_null',int(b.isna().sum()))
    if bad.any():
        print(M.loc[bad,['customer_id','as_of',f+'_live',f+'_off']].head(5).to_string(index=False))
